name: Low or No Background Audio
explanation: This criterion applies to prerecorded, speech-based audio — a podcast episode, an audiobook chapter, a recorded lecture — where music or ambient sound has been mixed in behind the narration. It requires one of three things: no background sound at all, a way to turn the background off separately from the speech, or a background mixed at least 20 decibels quieter than the speech (roughly four times quieter to the ear). A few things are exempt: brief incidental sounds, like a short sound logo at the start of an episode, and content where the 'background' sound is actually the point, like a recorded music performance. This criterion isn't about captions or transcripts — those are covered elsewhere and provide an alternative to the audio. It's about the raw audio mix itself: whether the speech is intelligible on its own.
whoItAffects: People who are hard of hearing benefit most directly. A mixed-in music bed can mask consonant sounds and make speech hard to distinguish, even at high volume, especially for listeners with high-frequency hearing loss. People with auditory processing disorders, some autistic listeners, and some people with cognitive disabilities can find it hard to separate simultaneous sounds, like foreground speech from background music, even with typical hearing — so an unclear mix can make an otherwise-accessible podcast effectively unusable. Older adults with age-related hearing decline, and anyone listening in a noisy environment like a train or open office, also benefit from a clean speech-to-background ratio or the ability to switch off the music bed entirely.

codeExample.bad: Episode 42: Interview with a Climate Scientist
codeExample.good:
Episode 42: Interview with a Climate Scientist

Lower this or set it to 0 to mute the background music bed while keeping the narration audible.

howToTest: Find a prerecorded, speech-based audio item on the site, such as a podcast episode, that has background music or ambient sound mixed in. Listen to a representative section with your eyes closed, focusing on whether you can follow every word of the narration without straining, even during the loudest part of the background sound. It fails if the background is distracting or occasionally drowns out a word, and there's no control to turn it off separately from the speech. Also check whether the site offers a volume control specifically for background music. If it does, verify it actually reduces the background rather than just lowering the whole mix, which would reduce the speech too.

check.question: A company publishes a spoken-word audiobook chapter with a quiet ambient music track mixed in behind the narrator. According to SC 1.4.7, which of these mixes would satisfy the criterion?
choices: The music is mixed at roughly the same volume as the narrator's voice
The music is at least 20 decibels quieter than the narration, or can be turned off separately from the speech
The music is provided as a separate download so listeners can play it if they want
Captions are provided alongside the audio, describing both the speech and the music
